Replying to: none
Cc: dm:moira.blyth
Subject: DRAFT for Moira to review – Light Up a Life 2026

Hilary Gotts asked on the page the other day whether we would be doing the tree again, because her mum’s name was on it last year. Yes, Hilary, we are. Please do bring your sister.

Our Light Up a Life tree will go into the shop window on Saturday 21 November. Memory tags will be available in the shop from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. There will be envelopes on the counter if you would rather take a tag home to write and bring it back. Write as much or as little as you wish. A name is quite enough.

We will switch the lights on on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are kindly coming back to sing three or four carols for us, and Doreen is making her mince pies again. Do wrap up warm and join us if you can.

This will be my seventh year of writing Ray’s name. He died at the hospice in November 2019. The first time I hung his tag, I could hardly write it. Now I write it here at the counter, with the same pen. It does not mean the seven years have not been long, or that I have stopped missing him. It only means that writing his name has become one of the ways I carry him with me.

The tree is for anyone who is grieving, not only for families who have been cared for by the hospice. Your person need not have died recently, and there is no right way to write a tag or to feel when you see it in the window. You are also very welcome simply to come in and stand beside the tree for a while. There is no need to buy anything, or to explain yourself to any of us.

All the names on the tags will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm in the hospice day centre. You do not have to attend the service for your person’s name to be included.

Thank you to everyone who remembered with us last year: all 412 names. Thank you for standing in the cold to hear the children sing, for trusting us with the people you love, and for the kindness you show one another in this little shop. We still have those tags kept safely together, and we still think of the people behind them.

Whether you write a tag every year, are thinking about your first, or simply want somewhere quiet to remember someone, you will be welcome here.

Jean

reasons: The piece says the tree goes in the window on Saturday 21 November, but Moira's message reads as the same Saturday as the 28 November switch-on, so the 21 November date is invented and likely wrong.
The post does not identify Ray as Jean’s husband.
